Subject: Re: Redwood demo + procurement path

Hi Susan —

Thanks again for taking time today. Quick recap from our discovery and clear next steps so procurement has what it needs: 

Summary from call:
- Primary use case: model serving for internal LLM features (chat + embeddings) with dedicated capacity.
- Volume estimate: ~2M tokens/month to start; traffic patterns steady daytime PST.
- Objectives: predictable latency, cost controls (batching/quantization), and SOC2/compliance evidence for vendor onboarding.

Procurement / commercial open questions (please confirm):
1) Preferred payment method: PO (Net30) vs corporate card? Which does ACME prefer for new vendors?
2) Approval & signatory path: who is the budget owner / economic buyer vs finance sponsor? Who signs contracts?
3) Marketplace interest: would ACME prefer to purchase via AWS Marketplace/partner route or direct Redwood invoice?
4) Typical procurement timeline & required docs (e.g., SOC2, IP addendum, insurance, W-9).

Attachments: pricing-proposal.pdf (attached) — includes tiered pricing and sample SOW language.

Proposed next steps:
- If possible, can you share the procurement checklist and the contact for the budget owner?
- I'll follow up with a short procurement readiness packet and a procurement-only call (15-20m) next week.

Thanks — looping in Vivek (solutions) and Aditya (enterprise ops) to help with legal/finance questions.

Best,
Marissa

Subject: Re: Redwood demo + procurement path

Hi Marissa —

Great to meet you and the team. Appreciate the clear recap. A few answers from procurement side: 

1) Payment method: For new vendors we prefer a PO / Net30 when possible. Card payments are acceptable for proof-of-concept purchases under $10k, but for production / reserved capacity deals we will go PO.

2) Approval path: Primary budget owner is Ellen Park (Head of AI). Finance sponsor is Liam O'Connor (CFO) for deals above $50k ARR; Liam is the final signatory for contracts. Procurement handles vendor onboarding and will request the standard packet.

3) Marketplace: We do prefer marketplace procurement for smaller subscriptions but for larger reserved capacity we typically do direct vendor contracts. Can you confirm if Redwood supports purchase via AWS Marketplace?

4) Required docs: SOC 2 Type II, insurance certificate, W-9, standard MSAs are required. Typical procurement timeline is 3–6 weeks once we have SOC2 and pricing and legal review begins.

I can share ACME's vendor checklist — attaching a redacted version is fine. Also happy to join a procurement readiness call next week.

Thanks,
Susan
Susan James
Senior Procurement Manager, ACME Corp
susan.james@acme.com

Thanks Susan — this is very helpful.

Confirming next items from our side:
- I'll send SOC2 Type II report and the insurance cert (we'll include W-9).
- Attaching a short SOW and pricing proposal that matches our demo configuration (redwood-sow.pdf + pricing-proposal.pdf).
- Redwood supports AWS Marketplace for certain SKUs; Vivek can confirm which reserved options map to Marketplace SKUs. If ACME prefers Marketplace we can provide that path; for reserved capacity customers we often recommend direct contract for better pricing/commit terms.

Can you share Ellen's preferred contact info so we can loop her into budget conversations? Also, can you confirm whether Liam needs line-item pricing for the finance review or a top-line committed spend figure?

Proposed times for a 20-minute procurement readiness call: Tue 4/21 10:00am PT or Wed 4/22 11:00am PT. What works best?

Marissa

+1 on the plan. A few internal notes for the thread:

- Net30 terms are standard for enterprise; we can offer Net45 or negotiated payment terms on annual commits.
- Marketplace: reserved capacity SKUs on AWS Marketplace are possible but pricing/commits differ; if ACME wants marketplace we'd need to map desired commit to SKU.

Marissa — if you confirm Ellen as budget owner and Liam as signatory, I'll prepare a short commercial summary (line items + recommended billing flow) for finance.
